newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips struggle higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips struggle higher at close.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa battled sellers and closed narrowly higher Tuesday, clinching its sixth consecutive gain on the back of strong economic indicators and lower U.S. long bond yields, dealers said.

"The market was very selective today, but managed to soak up profit-taking," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities. "Investors are betting on a MerVal of 730 and any drop is still regarded as a buying opportunity."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV erased slim losses and closed up 0.2 percent at 707.51. It stretched gains since its winning streak began last Tuesday to 7.8 percent.
The MerVal last stood at 700 three years ago and if it reaches 730 it would set a five-year high.
Traders said the market was cheered by stronger-than-expected January tax revenue, which should help ease the burden of Argentina's heavy 1997 debt repayments.
"Consumption is finally picking up as seen in the stronger tax collection, which means economic recovery has really shifted into high gear," another trader said.
Strength in the U.S. Treasuries market reflected confidence the Federal Open Market Committee would not touch interest rates when its meeting ends Wednesday, dealers said.
Bolsa gains were undercut by the telephone stocks, which snapped a two-day surge when the country's Ombudsman asked the courts Tuesday to revoke a recent tariff change, dealers said.
"The news halted the rally in the telephone sector, with some private pension funds reducing their exposure there," said Daneri.
The courts did not comment on the ombudsman's request.
However, Telefnica and Telecom slashed losses at the close to 0.3 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.
The broad market dipped 0.1 percent in the session, with rises beating declines 33 to 19 and 21 stocks closing flat.
Floor turnover picked up to 28.8 million pesos from 27.6 million Monday, while over-the-counter volume totaled 125.5 million pesos compared with 124.1 million Monday.
Best main-tier performers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas and steelmaker Siderca, both up 2.2 percent, and carmaker Sevel, up 1.9 percent.
Losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which tumbled 5.8 percent, and holding company Comercial del Plata and foods giant Molinos, off 1.7 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
